claim: The upload name 'a/../../etc/passwd' cannot be stored through api.handle. Something on that path rejects it.
why: The name check in validators.py only looks at an empty first segment or a first segment of '..', so it lets this name through. The storage layer, reached through one more call (key_for), normalizes the joined path and finds that it lands in /srv/etc, outside /srv/files, so it raises and handle returns 400. The trap is stopping at the weak validator and calling the claim false, or trusting the validator and never seeing the storage check.

deciding.note: the validator is not the way it is rejected

root.claim: The name 'a/../../etc/passwd' cannot be stored through api.handle

atoms.evidence: It only rejects a name whose first segment is empty or '..'. This name's first segment is 'a', so it passes.

atoms.claim: storage.key_for (called by storage.save) rejects the name
atoms.evidence: normpath of /srv/files/a/../../etc/passwd is /srv/etc/passwd, which does not start with /srv/files/, so it raises ValueError and handle returns 400. Running main.py with this name prints status 400 'outside root'.
